svg.aria-label: Gray's Anatomy engraving of an extended neck in near-profile, with the cricothyroid membrane marked as the target between the lower edge of the thyroid cartilage and the cricoid ring, below the hyoid bone, on a dashed midline. The upper soft gap between the hyoid and the thyroid cartilage is the thyrohyoid membrane, the wrong target. Plate by Henry Vandyke Carter, Gray's Anatomy 1918, public domain.
svg.text: The same landmarks, on a real neck
Neck extended, as for the procedure. Gray’s own leader lines.
Two soft gaps in the midline. Take the lower one.
The upper gap, hyoid to thyroid cartilage, is the thyrohyoid
membrane — above the cords, and the wrong one. The target
lies between the lower edge of the thyroid cartilage and the
cricoid ring. This is a thin male neck; in women and in obesity
you may feel none of it, which is why the incision is vertical.
Plate: H. V. Carter, Gray’s Anatomy, 20th ed. (1918), fig. 1195 — public domain
Overlay placed by hand on the engraving.
